Ready for the browser stores: sends from the popup no longer get lost, the extension claims only what it does, and the store kit is in the repository.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **A send from the popup could vanish without a trace.** The popup handed the send to the background worker and closed on the very next line. The worker goes to sleep about half a minute after the last activity, and when it was asleep the window was gone before it had started. Nothing arrived, and nothing said so. The popup now waits until the worker has taken the send and then closes, without waiting for the delivery itself.
- **Without a context-menu API the whole background stopped.** One unguarded menu call at the top of the background script threw, and the message listener below it was never registered, so every popup send was lost the same silent way. Browsers without menus now simply have no right-click entries.
- **Switching Click'n'Load off left the jdcheck.js rule running.** It went on answering sites' probes with a file from the extension. It now follows the switch, and is set again after every update, because a rule's on/off state does not survive one.
- **The popup said "Send this page" over a link it was about to send.** A right-clicked link, image or selection that needed a choice between instances opened the popup with the page title above that button. The button now names what is waiting: this link, this image, the selection, or these links for a caught Click'n'Load batch.
- **The popup read the current tab's address as soon as it opened.** It now reads it when you press send.
- **Leaving a group kept the browser ID**, so the same browser rejoined any group under the same ID. It is deleted with the phrase now.
- **Danish and Swedish called a text selection a committee and a sample.** Both use "markering" now, in the menu and in the popup.
- **Firefox was told the extension collects no data.** Mozilla counts anything handled outside the browser, including links sent to your own server and data that is encrypted on the way. The manifest now declares authentication info, browsing activity and website content, the same three things declared to the other stores, and Firefox shows them at install.
- **The privacy policy contradicted the extension.** It promised no identifiers and no code in the pages you visit. The rewrite describes the browser ID, every hook of the Click'n'Load script, the link collector, what the relay keeps and for how long, your choices, and who is responsible.

## 🔧 Changed

- **No more `activeTab`.** The access to all websites that Click'n'Load needs already lets the popup read the current tab, and Chrome's review treats `activeTab` next to it as a permission the extension does not need.
- **Firefox 140 on desktop, not offered on Android.** The minimum was 142 before, which shut out Firefox ESR 140. Firefox for Android has no context menus and the extension was never tested there, so AMO lists it for desktop only.

## ✨ Added

- **`extension/store/`**: listing texts, permission justifications, data answers and reviewer notes for all three stores in `SUBMISSION.md`, the store icon, logo and promo tiles with their generator, four screenshots, a test page for reviewers and a 47-second walkthrough video. No browser is named in the listing texts or the images, because Edge rejects listings that mention another one.
- **Two new CI checks.** `check-popup-send.mjs` holds the send label, the tab read on send and the hand-over before the popup closes. `check-background.mjs` loads the background scripts against a stubbed browser, once without context menus, and holds the jdcheck.js rule to the switch.
